triggers: a kernel on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942) risks the '5. Deferred per-dc rescale interleaved with MFMA regresses vs all-upfront' trap

payload.goal: Avoid a known trap on AMD MI308X (CDNA3 / gfx942): 5. Deferred per-dc rescale interleaved with MFMA regresses vs all-upfront

problem.statement: Pitfalls: FlyDSL Flash Attention on MI308X (gfx942) -- 5. Deferred per-dc rescale interleaved with MFMA regresses vs all-upfront

payload.attempted: Sage V9 says "delay O rescaling — `o_accs[1..3]` rescale at PV sub-tile 0 setup". Sounds like the rescale should be tucked inside the MFMA loop at the (dc==k, pks==0) boundary so the MULs overlap with in-flight MFMAs.
payload.lesson: "deferred rescale" is shape-dependent. The benefit is overlapping the rescale VALU with prior MFMAs; if your loop already has a long stretch of uninterrupted MFMAs and you don't have register pressure, doing the rescales upfront is simpler and faster.

established_fact.mechanism: with the v6 pre-load-V structure, the MUL is no longer naturally adjacent to a free VALU slot. Putting the conditional `if pks==0 and dc>0:` inside the loop creates a per-iter branch that the compiler can't eliminate cleanly. Doing all rescales BEFORE the MFMA loop lets them hoist outside any in-flight MFMA dependency.
